results.title: Ramified primes divide the discriminant
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n\ge1$, $\mathcal O$ the ring of integers of $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$, $p$ a prime and $P$ a maximal ideal of $\mathcal O$ lying over $p$ with $P^2=p\mathcal O$. Then $p\mid n$, or $p=2$ and $n\equiv1\pmod4$.

results.summary: For a natural number $n$, let $T_n$ be the set of prime factors of $n$ (empty for $n=0$) if $n\equiv3\pmod4$, and that set together with $2$ otherwise; write $t=|T_n|$. Every element of $T_n$ is prime, and every prime factor of $n$ lies in $T_n$. Motivation: for odd squarefree $n$, $T_n$ is the set of primes dividing the discriminant of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$, and these are exactly the primes that ramify there.

results.title: The primes of the discriminant ramify
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ be odd and squarefree and $p\in T_n$. Then $\mathfrak p_p$ is maximal, $\mathfrak p_p^2=p\mathcal O$ and $N(\mathfrak p_p)=p$. Moreover $\mathfrak p_p$ is the only prime ideal of $\mathcal O$ lying over $p$, and every automorphism of $K$ fixes $\mathfrak p_p$.

results.title: An ideal times its conjugate is generated by its norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n\ge1$, $\mathcal O$ the ring of integers of $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ and $\sigma$ the nontrivial automorphism. Every ideal $I$ of $\mathcal O$ satisfies the principal ideal generated by the natural number $N(I)$. Consequently $N(\tau I)=N(I)$ for every automorphism $\tau$ of $K$ and every ideal $I$.
